results.title: 2026 banking and capital markets outlook | Deloitte Insights
results.content: Corporate borrowers could enjoy lower rates, reversing the 5.6% drop in the volume of commercial and industrial loans in the first half of the year.[14](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-outlooks/banking-industry-outlook.html#endnote-14) Spending on AI and data centers would likely keep demand for debt relatively high, even from the most cash-rich companies. For example, capital and liquidity rules have forced some banks to consolidate risk data and establish lineage; stress-testing regimes such as the Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR) and the Dodd-Frank Act Stress Test (DFAST) have driven more timely, auditable data sets; and AML and sanctions reporting have required standardized customer and transaction data.[67](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-outlooks/banking-industry-outlook.html#endnote-67) But, these investments often remain siloed, serving only their original compliance mandate rather than being scaled into a foundation that could power AI across the enterprise. For instance, banks like BNY are using external sources such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s AI risk management framework to align their use of data across the AI life cycle.[68](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-outlooks/banking-industry-outlook.html#endnote-68).
